formula: mean(ttl) over IP packets in window
expected_information: high — mean hop distance shifts when the remote peer population changes
reason: Primary TTL location statistic; no V4 analogue exists at any level.

expected_information: high — separates a single-origin window from a many-origin window
reason: Dispersion is orthogonal to the mean; 0.0 for constant TTL is a meaningful state.

expected_information: medium — tracks the most distant observed source
redundancy_risk: medium — correlated with the mean when dispersion is low
reason: Kept: min and max bracket the hop-distance range, which mean+std alone cannot recover for a multi-modal TTL mix (the normal case: local 64/128 plus remote ~45-55).

expected_information: medium — tracks nearest / locally originated traffic
reason: Kept for the same bracketing reason as ttl_min.

expected_information: high — fan-out / spoofing indicator independent of the location statistics
reason: Diversity, not location; the only TTL feature that responds to a scan fan-out while the mean stays flat.

expected_information: low — nearly identical to ttl_mean on real TTL distributions
redundancy_risk: HIGH — redundant with ttl_mean and bracketed by ttl_min/ttl_max
reason: REJECTED. TTL is an 8-bit field with a handful of modes (64/128/255 minus hop count); a median adds no shape information the mean plus the min/max bracket does not already carry. Percentiles are justified for payload length, which is genuinely long-tailed, not for TTL.

expected_information: low
reason: REJECTED for the same reason as ttl_p50; ttl_max already covers the upper end.

formula: entropy of the TTL value distribution
expected_information: medium
redundancy_risk: HIGH — log_ttl_unique_count captures the same diversity more cheaply
reason: REJECTED. Entropy and unique-count move together for a field with <= 256 values and few modes; one diversity feature per family is enough.

expected_information: high — receiver flow-control level
reason: Primary window location statistic; log-compressed because the field is heavy-tailed (0 to 65535).

expected_information: high — heterogeneity of peer buffer states
reason: Orthogonal to the mean; distinguishes one steady peer from many varied peers.

expected_information: medium — upper extent of advertised receive capacity
reason: Kept: the maximum is set by the most capable receiver and is stable, which makes it a useful scale reference for the mean.

expected_information: low — almost always 0 or near 0 in any busy window
redundancy_risk: HIGH — determined by tcp_window_zero_ratio whenever any zero-window packet is present
reason: REJECTED. In a window containing even one zero-window advertisement the minimum is exactly 0, so the feature degenerates into a worse-behaved copy of tcp_window_zero_ratio, which reports the same event with magnitude.

expected_information: high — explicit receiver stall, a distinct network state
reason: Selected over the raw count: the count is confounded with traffic volume, which log_total_packets already carries.

expected_information: medium
reason: REJECTED in favour of the ratio. The count cannot be read without simultaneously reading a volume feature, which defeats the point of a compact representation.

formula: count(window differs from same-session predecessor) / count(TCP packets with a predecessor)
expected_information: high — congestion dynamics that no level statistic can express
reason: Selected. The denominator is packets WITH a predecessor, not all TCP packets, so the first packet of every session is excluded from both terms.

expected_information: high IF fragmentation occurs — fragmentation floods and MTU-evasion are real techniques
pcap_available: yes (parsable) / NO VARIANCE (zero in every available capture)
reason: Selected on correctness grounds despite being identically zero in the data available here. The problem statement names fragmentation explicitly; the family is implemented, fixture-verified against synthetic fragments, and will populate on any capture that contains fragments. Its degeneracy in this dataset is reported, not hidden.

expected_information: high IF fragmentation occurs
reason: Kept alongside the count: the count detects a fragmentation flood in a busy window, the ratio detects a small but wholly fragmented conversation.

expected_information: medium — path-MTU-discovery behaviour and OS/stack mix
reason: Selected. The only fragmentation-family feature with real variance in the available captures, and semantically part of the IP fragmentation control field.

expected_information: medium
redundancy_risk: HIGH — a strict subset of frag_packet_ratio (which also counts last fragments)
reason: REJECTED. Splitting the already-empty fragmentation signal into MF-only and offset-only halves would add dead dimensions without adding a distinguishable state.

expected_information: low — only meaningful once fragmentation exists at all
reason: REJECTED. Third-order detail of a family that is empty in this dataset.

formula: log1p(count of seq-bearing TCP packets re-covering already-sent sequence space)
expected_information: high — loss, congestion and scan retry behaviour
pcap_available: yes — 1.4% of seq-bearing packets, present in 24% of windows on real traffic
reason: Selected. Detection uses TCP sequence semantics (eff_len = payload + SYN + FIN) with 32-bit modular comparison; zero-length packets are excluded so duplicate ACKs are never counted.

expected_information: high — scale-free retransmission intensity
reason: Kept: separates 'a few retransmissions in a huge window' from 'a small window that is mostly retransmission'. Denominator is seq-bearing packets, not all TCP packets.

expected_information: medium — separates cheap control retry from expensive bulk retry
redundancy_risk: medium — correlated with the count when payloads are uniform
reason: Kept for one specific reason: SYN/FIN retransmission produces count > 0 with bytes == 0, a distinction the count alone destroys and which matters for scan traffic.

expected_information: none beyond the count
redundancy_risk: TOTAL — an exact affine transform of the count (count / 10)
reason: REJECTED. Dividing a per-window count by the constant window width is a rescaling, not a new feature; it is exactly collinear with log_tcp_retrans_count's argument.

expected_information: medium — a genuine loss signal
reason: REJECTED for this version. A defensible duplicate-ACK rule needs the ACK number plus SACK-option parsing to avoid counting window updates and keepalives; the parser does not read TCP options, so the rule would be approximate. Deferred rather than shipped weak.

formula: count of packets arriving below the high-water mark
expected_information: medium
redundancy_risk: TOTAL — under a high-water-mark rule this is the SAME population as the retransmission count
reason: REJECTED. Without RTT and duplicate-ACK context, reordering and retransmission are the same observation. Shipping both names for one measurement would be misleading; the single feature is documented as 'sequence-space re-coverage' instead.

expected_information: high — robust typical message size
reason: Selected as a ROBUST centre, which a mean is not. V4's mean_pkt_len is a mean-of-flow-means and is dragged by a single bulk flow; a median is not.

expected_information: high — upper-tail shape, separates bulk transfer from control chatter
reason: Selected. Together with p50 this IS the 'richer payload-size distribution' the problem statement asks for, and neither is reachable from V4's mean/std pair.

expected_information: medium — MTU / TSO segment ceiling
reason: Kept: the gap between p90 and max is itself informative, and the max exposes TSO/LRO-coalesced segments that reveal where the capture was taken.

expected_information: high — ACK-dominated vs data-dominated traffic
reason: Selected. No V4 feature distinguishes an empty window of ACKs from a window of small writes; both give a small mean packet length.

expected_information: none
reason: REJECTED. Exactly 1 - payload_zero_ratio; carries no information any model cannot already reach.

formula: Shannon entropy (base 2) of the payload LENGTH distribution
expected_information: high — a collapse to uniform message sizes is the fixed-size beacon signature
reason: Selected. Explicitly a LENGTH-distribution entropy, computed with the same formula V4 uses for dst_port_entropy. It is NOT byte-value entropy and reads no payload byte.

expected_information: medium
redundancy_risk: HIGH — V4 mean_pkt_len already carries a mean of the same underlying quantity (mean-of-flow-means); the two differ only in weighting
reason: REJECTED to avoid duplicating a feature the flow lane already provides. Part 11 explicitly forbids duplicating a feature because both lanes can compute it. p50 is kept instead because a robust centre is genuinely different from a mean.

expected_information: medium
redundancy_risk: HIGH — V4 std_pkt_len is the flow-lane version of the same spread
reason: REJECTED for the same duplication reason; the p50/p90/max triple describes the spread with shape information a single std cannot express.

expected_information: none — 0 in essentially every real window
reason: REJECTED. Constant 0 on all real traffic; payload_zero_ratio reports the same fact with magnitude.

formula: Shannon entropy of the payload BYTE VALUES
expected_information: high for encryption/compression detection — but a DIFFERENT question
computational_cost: HIGH — requires reading and histogramming every payload byte
reason: REJECTED on scope and cost. This is content inspection, which Part 7 rules out, and it answers a different question from payload-size distribution. It is also the concept most often confused with payload_len_entropy; the two are deliberately not conflated.
